title: GHz silicon modulator
title_note: The paper makes no "first" claim. It says the fastest silicon-waveguide modulator demonstrated before reached only about 20 MHz (its refs 10, 11) and calls 1 GHz "the benchmark figure" (Liu et al., Nature 2004, p.615, p.617). MOS = metal-oxide-semiconductor; CMOS = complementary MOS. No Supplementary Information is published with this Letter.
tagline: A MOS capacitor in a silicon waveguide modulates light beyond 1 GHz.

parts.name: p-type polysilicon rib
parts.role: Upper capacitor electrode and the rib that guides the light
parts.detail: A "p-type doped polysilicon rib" on the gate oxide: about 2.5 µm wide, about 0.9 µm thick at the waveguide centre, active doping about 3 × 10^{16} cm^{−3}. Amorphous silicon deposited by low-pressure chemical vapour deposition at 550 °C, then crystallized by a high-temperature anneal designed to minimize grain boundaries. The rib gives the horizontal confinement; about 9 % of the TE power lies in the polysilicon (simulation). Single-mode around 1.55 µm.

parts.name: Accumulated charge
parts.role: Thin charge layers on both sides of the gate oxide; drawn 60 nm each, 6 times the 10 nm effective thickness
parts.detail: "When a positive voltage V_{D} is applied to the device, a thin charge layer is accumulated on both sides of the gate oxide": holes in the polysilicon, electrons in the silicon. Eq. (1): ΔN_{e} = ΔN_{h} = ε_{0}ε_{r}(V_{D} − V_{FB}) / (e t_{ox} t), with V_{FB} = 1.25 V and t = 10 nm from the device simulation. Majority carriers only: no slow generation or recombination. Sheets drawn far thicker than 10 nm; no charge below V_{FB}.

chapters.line: An all-silicon modulator made in a CMOS production facility.
chapters.action: finished MZI chip (schematic plan, shortened) floats in, tilted; light runs through both arms; slow drift

chapters.line: An n-type silicon layer on a thin buried oxide.
chapters.action: camera dives to a cut through one phase shifter; the chip dissolves to the substrate; buried oxide and the 1.4 um n-type slab settle on it (cross-section to scale); the two n-Si contact regions shade in at the slab ends

chapters.line: A thin oxide under the rib, just as wide.
chapters.action: macro on the slab centre; a 2.5 um wide oxide sheet appears (thickness exaggerated, hover says so); pull back. Assembly order is for the picture only (the paper gives no process flow)

chapters.line: A p-type polysilicon rib between oxide blocks guides the light.
chapters.action: oxide blocks settle on both sides of the gate oxide, then the polysilicon rib and the wide polysilicon layer drop in as one piece (layers of the cross-section, no process order); no mode spot (withheld)

chapters.line: Aluminium contacts sit off to the side, away from the light.
chapters.action: outer polysilicon shades to the doped colour; two aluminium contacts land beside the rib; V_D lead and ground marker appear as in Fig. 1

chapters.line: Positive drive gathers charge on both sides of the oxide.
chapters.action: drive ramps from 0 to 10 V (top of the Fig. 2 range); no charge until 1.25 V (flat band), then hole sheet above and electron sheet below the gate oxide brighten in proportion to V_D - 1.25 V (Eq. 1); sheets exaggerated in thickness

chapters.line: Identical phase shifters in both arms of an asymmetric interferometer.
chapters.action: the cross-section extrudes along z into a phase shifter; camera pulls back; a second shifter, plain passive guides and the two Y junctions complete the schematic MZI (plan shortened); light enters, splits and recombines

chapters.line: Phase grows almost linearly with drive voltage and with length.
chapters.action: plots.phase assembles; model left half, one phase shifter alone (Fig. 2 was measured in a free-space interferometer, not the MZI); V_D follows the plot pen from 1 to 10 V; wave crests in the shifter slide by the 8 mm measured phase (the plotted point); charge sheets follow V_D but are not visible at this scale

chapters.line: Driving one arm swings the output through interference.
chapters.action: plots.transfer assembles; model left half, whole MZI; V_D on one shifter follows the pen (about 1.0 to 13.7 V); output brightness = 10^(dB/10) of the digitized curve at the pen voltage (darkest near 1.9 V, brightest near 9.4 V)

chapters.line: Optical response holds up past the gigahertz benchmark.
chapters.action: plots.response assembles (alternate Fig. 4a on the toggle); model left half, MZI with a single shifter in one arm (other arm plain, hover says this is a different device with one 2.5 mm shifter); sine drive whose frequency follows the pen (0.1 to 3.2 GHz, held at the end); output modulation depth = 10^(y/10) of the plotted response (equal to the Fig. 4a voltage ratio); orbit and explode offered
